subject: forensic-medicine
title: Death and early postmortem changes

steps.tx: **Death** is studied under thanatology, the science of death in all its aspects. Death is staged. **Somatic death** is the complete, irreversible stoppage of circulation, breathing and brain function. **Molecular death** is the death of individual cells and tissues, and it lags behind somatic death. Tissues die at different times, which is why organ retrieval windows differ. Cornea can be used up to about 6 hours after death, while bone and vessels remain usable for much longer.

Tissues die at different times, which is why organ retrieval windows differ. Cornea can be used up to about six hours after death, while bone and vessels remain usable for much longer.

rows: Irreversible loss of circulation, breathing, brain
Loss of all brain and brainstem function

steps.tx: **Suspended animation** is apparent death, not true death. Signs of life are reduced to a minimum, but the person can still be resuscitated. It is seen in electrocution, apparent drowning, cerebral concussion, deep shock, and after anaesthesia. **Brain death** is different. Brainstem function is lost permanently, and the criteria must hold for a set period, with certification by independent physicians. Brain death is a legal and clinical diagnosis, not simple unconsciousness.

steps.tx: **Algor mortis** is the cooling of the body after death, caused by stoppage of heat production. It is the most useful single indicator of time since death during the first 24 hours in temperate climates. Rectal temperature is the ideal site, since it hardly falls for the first half to one hour. In tropical climates the fall is minimal, so the method is less reliable there. Postmortem caloricity is the opposite: the temperature stays raised for about two hours after death in sunstroke, tetanus, strychnine poisoning and septicaemia.

rows: About 1.5 F per hour in temperate climate

steps.tx: **Heat stiffening** mimics rigor and occurs when muscle proteins are denatured, usually above 60 degrees Celsius. **Cold stiffening** is a different phenomenon. Rigor mortis is simulated by these conditions, but not by putrefaction. Lividity, or **livor mortis**, is the dark purple discolouration from gravitational pooling of blood in dependent parts. It is fixed in about four to six hours and maximal at six to twelve hours. It does not form in areas of contact flattening.

Putrefaction does not simulate rigor. Livor mortis is the dark purple discolouration from gravitational pooling of blood in dependent parts. It becomes fixed in about four to six hours and is maximal at six to twelve hours. It does not form in areas of contact flattening.

steps.tx: Eye changes help estimate time after death. The **Kevorkian sign** is fragmentation of the blood column in retinal vessels, appearing within minutes and lasting about an hour. **Tache noire** forms as two yellow triangles on the sclera, later turning brown then black, when the eyes stay open. Vitreous humour is the best fluid for estimating postmortem interval, with potassium being the most useful component. Urine is not studied for this purpose.
